title: Promotion decision — candidate (arch-20-noreg) vs rule-basis & Run3 schema-4, fresh v5fh holdout
protocol: paired-holdout, v5fh seeds (disjoint from training/curriculum), 3 modes x 2 maps x 2 opponents x 2 pairs = 24 matches/mode, 72 total; observation unit = match; 95% paired CI
promotionRule: Promote only if, per mode, gateEvaluate passes AND negative gates clear AND the paired win advantage over BOTH baselines is distinguishable from 0 (win.n>=5, ciLow>0). 0/0 or not-distinguishable never promotes. Run3 stays ACTIVE unless the overall decision is eligible.

offlineVsLive.source: s6-decision-capture/decision-impact.json (12 scenarios, same bot source, per-frame capture)
offlineVsLive.note: The offline within-frame decision rate (17.96%) collapses to ~2% live after the gain-18 control gate + safety gate, and the live changes produce zero end-land difference vs the rule baseline in every scenario.

decision.reason: Not eligible in any of the 3 modes. In every mode the candidate's endLand is exactly equal to rule-basis (land CI [0,0]) and the paired win advantage over BOTH baselines is not distinguishable from 0 (win CI [0,0] or n=1). The strict paired gate returns valid=false (incomplete-recording-or-unverified: tick-limit censored matches) in all 3 modes. 0/0 and not-distinguishable never promote.
decision.verdict: Deliver the best fully-checked candidate (arch-20-noreg) as the improved schema-5 line; it is a genuine offline improvement (cross-std 0.5031, 6x offline decision rate vs full-batch M2) but does NOT yet demonstrate a decisive live win advantage over rule-basis or the Run3 schema-4 champion. Run3 remains the ACTIVE champion.

decisiveBottleneck.name: offline-to-live binding gap: the gain-18 control gate + safety gate admit only ~2% of the model's offline-decided changes, and those changes do not move end land
evidence: Offline (held-out val): within-frame decision rate 0.1796, cross-candidate score spread 0.5031 (arch-20-noreg).
Live (12 scenarios): changedRate 0.0201 (~9x lower); schema-5 endLand == rule-basis endLand in 12/12 scenarios (mean 95605.6, land delta exactly 0).
Holdout (24/mode): candidate endLand CI vs rule-basis is [0,0] in all 3 modes; paired win advantage vs both baselines not distinguishable (win CI [0,0] / n=1).
Heavy tick-limit censoring (7/8 in 1v1) makes the strict gate invalid and leaves too few decisive pairs to resolve a win advantage.
decisiveBottleneck.nextLever: The lever is the control GAIN / safety-gate threshold (and possibly the score-to-utility calibration), NOT more training: the model already produces a 0.5031 within-frame spread offline, but the live gate rarely admits it and the admitted changes are land-neutral. A targeted study of the live rule-utility gap vs the model score spread (per frame, at gain 18) is the next experiment.
